newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives go to battle on education.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives go to battle on education.

text.p: Britain's ruling Conservative Party on Wednesday used its election manifesto to open up education as a key campaign issue, pledging to set targets for schools and to act against those that underperform.
The party's manifesto said national targets would be set to ensure Britain "is in the top league of international standards".
Every school would be required to produce plans to improve performance, parents will be fully informed and any school not coming up to scratch will have action taken against it, the manifesto said.
Testing of children will be widened. "We will publish all school test results including the results of tests of seven- and 14-year olds. We propose also to assess every child at five."
A new test for 14 year-olds will be phased in, aimed at gauging progress across the whole National Curriculum before choices of GCSE exam subjects are made.

The Tories also pledged to set up a more rigorous system for appraising teachers and said it would allow independent inspection of education authorities with the power to intervene directly to raise standards.
Opposition Labour Party leader Tony Blair has already promised to make education the central issue of the campaign.
The election will be held on May 1. The Conservatives lag badly in the polls although the latest polls suggest the gap may be narrowing.
